items.title: Public authority can’t be forced to get info from third parties for RTI applicants: Bombay High Court
items.summary: The Bombay High Court on Tuesday ruled that a public authority is under no legal obligation under the Right to Information Act, 2005 (RTI Act) to collect or obtain information from a private body merely to furnish it to an RTI applicant [ Securities and Exchange Board of India v. Yogesh Mehta & Ors. ]. A Division Bench of Justices Manish Pitale and Shreeram V Shirsat made the observation while quashing certain orders passed by the Central Information Commission (CIC). The CIC had directed the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to collect certain information from the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), so that the same may be given to RTI applicants. SEBI and BSE challenged such directives before the High Court. Granting them relief, the Court held, "The provisions (of the RTI Act) do not indicate that a public authority, like SEBI in the present case, which is a regulatory body empowered to call upon third parties to provide information in terms of its own governing statute, is under an obligation to obtain information from third parties to satisfy persons applying for such information." items.title: ‘File a case against Gandhi, Nehru,’: Kharge challenges BJP govt over Vande Mataram law
items.summary: Congress national president Mallikarjun Kharge on Tuesday, August 18, challenged the Narendra Modi government to file a case against him, as well as Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, if singing the version of Vande Mataram traditionally used by the Congress amounts to an offence under the amended national honour law. The Congress has traditionally sang only the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram following its 1937 CWC resolution. The national song, written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, had remained controversial over its religious references. While its first two stanzas are an invocation of the motherland, the later stanzas describe the motherland using imagery associated with Hindu goddesses, including Durga, leading to objections by a section of Muslims. During the freedom movement, leaders including Gandhi and Rabindranath Tagore had supported limiting public renditions to the first two stanzas to not alienate the Muslims. items.title: 1 takedown order every 68 seconds: Union issued 1.95 lakh blocking orders in 5 months
items.summary: The Union government issued nearly 1.95 lakh blocking orders to Instagram, Facebook and YouTube between March and July, averaging about 1,275 orders a day, or roughly one order every 68 seconds, according to data accessed by The Indian Express . The blocking directives represented a sharp increase compared with the 2,312 orders sent to 19 online platforms through the government’s Sahyog portal between October 2024 and October 2025. That earlier figure translated to an average of about six blocking orders a day. Instagram received the largest share of the latest directives, with nearly one lakh orders during the five-month period. Facebook received around 80,000, while YouTube received nearly 15,000. Together, Meta-owned Instagram and Facebook accounted for roughly nine out of every 10 orders issued to the three platforms. Each blocking order can cover hundreds of individual posts, pieces of content or accounts. Most of the orders were issued by central and state agencies through the Union Home Ministry’s Sahyog portal. items.title: Goa govt moves SC seeking life sentence for Tarun Tejpal in 2013 rape case
items.summary: The Goa government has approached the Supreme Court seeking life imprisonment for former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal, challenging the 10-year sentence imposed on him by the Bombay High Court in the 2013 rape case, Live Law reported . In its petition, the State has made it clear that it is not challenging Tarun Tejpal’s conviction or seeking to reopen the findings recorded by the High Court. Its challenge is limited to the quantum of punishment. “The challenge is confined to the quantum of sentence and the direction for concurrent operation of sentences,” the State said, arguing that the sentence imposed by the High Court was “manifestly inadequate”, the petition says, according to Bar and Bench. The case dates back to November 2013, when Tarun Tejpal was accused of sexually assaulting a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator in Goa during Tehelka’s annual ThinkFest event. Goa Police subsequently registered an FIR against him for offences including rape. He was arrested in November 2013 and released on bail in July 2014. items.title: Hyderabad woman dies after RMP allegedly administers injection; probe ordered
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A 30-year-old woman in Hyderabad died on Tuesday, August 18, after allegedly receiving an injection from a Rural Medical Practitioner (RMP) in Karwan Vaddera Basti, prompting an inquiry by the Ranga Reddy district medical and health officer (DMHO). The woman, identified as Srilatha, was a daily wage worker. She had developed a fever and consulted an RMP, identified as Ashok, in her locality on Friday, August 14. According to reports, Ashok examined her and administered an injection in her lower back before sending her home. RMPs are not qualified to practise modern medicine independently and do not hold medical licences that permit them to prescribe modern drugs or perform medical procedures. Despite this, they remain widely relied upon for primary healthcare in several parts of Telangana. On August 15, Srilatha developed swelling and severe pain in her legs. When her condition did not improve, she returned to Ashok on Monday, August 17. He subsequently took her to Zoi Hospital, where she was admitted for treatment. items.title: CCPA imposes ₹1 lakh penalty on Amazon for allowing sale of ordinary sweets as Ram Mandir Prasad
items.summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of ₹1 lakh on Amazon Seller Services Private Limited for allowing ordinary sweets to be sold on its platform as “Shri Ram Mandir Ayodhya Prasad” without authorisation from the Ram Mandir Trust. The CCPA observed that 'Shri Ram Mandir Ayodhya Prasad' would ordinarily be understood by devotees as food offered to and blessed by the deity at the Ayodhya Ram temple. “The commercial appropriation of this phrase for ordinary confectionery products, without any authorization from the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, constitutes not just a misleading trade practice under the CP Act but an affront to the religious sentiments of crores of consumers ,” the order stated. The CCPA held that Amazon was party to the publication of misleading advertisements since it hosted, displayed and facilitated the sale of the products, and it could not claim safe harbour protection available to intermediaries under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act (IT Act).
